# Module — `src/modules/billing/`

## Purpose
PAYG Flow wallet, subscription billing, and Stitch Express payments. Owns mutations of `flow_wallet`, `flow_ledger`, `flow_purchases`, and the recurring-debit lifecycle. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-19-payg-flows-pricing-design.md`.

## Services

| Service | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `flowOperationCatalog.ts` | Single source of truth for Flow costs per operation code (`bank.import`=1, `invoice.create`=3, `report.tb`=10, `afs.generate`=50). Categories: `basic` / `standard` / `advanced` / `premium`. |
| `flowWalletService.ts` (+ `flowWalletTx.ts`, `flowWalletMutations.ts`, `flowPurchaseService.ts`, re-exported) | Wallet CRUD + ledger writes. Every mutation (`deductFlows`, `refundFlows`, `setAutoTopup`, the bundle-purchase start/complete/fail paths, `recalculateNudge`, `resetMonthlyCounter`) runs in its own migration_admin transaction via `migrationAdminSqlTx` (S-07e, migration 945: no app role writes the Flows tables); each COMMITs on its own, not with the request. `adminAdjust` alone stays on `withTransaction` (the platform_admin request). `getWallet` lists its columns: `payment_method_token` is unreadable to app roles. |
| `stitchClient.ts` | Stitch Express REST client (NOT GraphQL). OAuth2 `client_credentials` → bearer token cached in-memory; cache invalidated 60s before expiry. |
| `paystackClient.ts` | Paystack REST client entry point: a barrel that re-exports `paystackTransactions.ts` (initialise / verify / charge authorization) and `paystackSubscriptions.ts` (plans, subscriptions); the shared request core (`paystackFetch`, base URL, env) is `paystackHttp.ts`. Import from `paystackClient`, never the parts (a `vi.mock` of the barrel only intercepts the barrel). The import rule is an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` (+ dynamic `import()`) in `eslint.config.mjs`; `tests/` and `scripts/` are not linted, so it does not cover them. The export surface is pinned by `tests/unit/services/billing/paystackClientExports.test.ts`. |
| `paystackMandateActivation.ts` | Promotes a captured Paystack authorization onto the mandate its checkout was started for. Shared by the `charge.success` webhook handler and `POST /api/billing/paystack/mandate/verify` (owner/admin, CSRF; audit K-202) so the two cannot drift. |
| `subscriptionBillingService.ts` | Recurring-debit lifecycle: `generateDueCharges` (queue) → `runQueuedCharges` (execute via `debitFromMandate`). |
| `subscriptionBillingService.ts` | Recurring-debit lifecycle: `generateDueCharges` (queue a charge per due subscription, then void/close-out subscriptions flagged `cancel_at_period_end`) → `runQueuedCharges` (claim the attempt, then execute via Paystack `chargeAuthorization`). |
| `subscriptionPeriod.ts` | Subscription period transitions, shared by the cron and the Paystack webhook: `advancePeriodForSettledCharge`, `settleSubscriptionCharge`, `markPastDueIfExhausted`, `voidChargesForCancellingSubscriptions`, `closeOutCancelledSubscriptions`, plus `MAX_ATTEMPTS`. |

## Caller contract
- Wrapped metered API routes call `getFlowCost(code)` from `flowOperationCatalog` — NEVER hard-code Flow integers in route handlers.
- Wallet mutations always take `companyId` first; routes live under `pages/api/billing/`.
- Admin routes for plan/invoice/PAYG management live under `pages/api/admin/billing/`.
- Buying Flows (`POST /api/billing/flows/purchase`) and auto top-up (`PATCH /api/billing/flows/auto-topup`) are owner/admin only: `withWriteAccess(handler, { allowedRoles: ['owner', 'admin'] })`: the company roles the mandate routes' `withRole('admin')` admits, without that hierarchy's `system`/`super_admin`. The Flows page and `FlowWalletWidget` disable their controls for other roles; the 403 is the control.

## Main function signatures (verified against source)
- `getWallet(companyId) → FlowWallet | null`
- `deductFlows(companyId, flowCost, operationCode, referenceId?)` — balance↓ + `debit` ledger row in one migration_admin transaction that COMMITs on its own (the request's rollback does not undo it: `withFlowMeter`/MCP refund on failure, and `runAfterRollback` refunds when the request rolls back after a 2xx); throws `InsufficientFlowsError` when balance < flowCost.
- `refundFlows(companyId, flowCost, operationCode, referenceId?)` — atomic balance↑ + `refund` ledger row; also unwinds `month_flows_used` so the nudge isn't punished. **Note:** the caller passes the refund cost — this is NOT a "reverse-by-ledger-id" helper.
- `adminAdjust(companyId, flows, reason)` — emergency credit/debit (`flows` non-zero integer); writes `admin_adjustment` ledger row.
- `startBundlePurchase / completeBundlePurchase / completePaidBundlePurchase / failBundlePurchase / getPurchaseStatus` — purchase lifecycle. The webhook credits only through `completePaidBundlePurchase` (its company, at least its price, in ZAR); `completeBundlePurchase` (no payment check) is the dev-only unpaid fallback's.
- `triggerAutoTopup(companyId)` — separate function, NOT auto-invoked inside `deductFlows`. Returns `AutoTopupResult` with `reason` ∈ `disabled | no_payment_method | no_bundle`. v1 has no gateway, so it NEVER credits: enabled with a bundle answers `no_payment_method`.
- `setAutoTopup(companyId, enabled, bundleId)` — sets the auto-topup flag/bundle. Does NOT update `payment_method_token`.
- `recalculateNudge(companyId) → NudgeLevel` — `none|yellow|orange|red` based on `month_flows_used`.
- `resetMonthlyCounter()` — cron tick that resets `month_flows_used` for all companies.
- `createPaymentLink(amount, reference, redirectUrl)` / `getPaymentStatus(paymentId)` — Stitch.
- `debitFromMandate(input: DebitFromMandateInput)` — single-object arg (`bankAccountId`, `amountCents`, `currency?`, `payerReference`, `beneficiaryReference`, `externalReference`); returns `Promise<never>` — currently always throws (see Gotchas).
- `generateDueCharges(now?)` / `runQueuedCharges(now?)` — subscription cron.

## Business rules
- Ledger types: `purchase | debit | refund | admin_adjustment`. Each balance-changing function writes one ledger row; `recalculateNudge` and `failBundlePurchase` change non-balance state and write no ledger row.
- Nudge levels are recomputed on every deduct/refund and exposed via `recalculateNudge`. **Auto-topup is a v2 hook**: callers that want auto-topup must explicitly invoke `triggerAutoTopup` (e.g. from a route after `deductFlows` raises `InsufficientFlowsError`). It is not fired inside `deductFlows`.
- Subscription charge state: `queued → succeeded | failed`. `failed` rows are retried up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` with `RETRY_BACKOFF_HOURS=24` backoff.
- **A paystack authorisation activates exactly ONE mandate: the one its checkout was started for.** `paystack_payment_requests.mandate_id` (migration 651) records the link; rows written before it are NULL and fall back to the company's newest pending/active paystack mandate. `resolveAuthorisedMandate` / `activateAuthorisedMandate` in `paystackMandateActivation.ts` are the only sanctioned way to do this — do not re-open a company-wide `UPDATE subscription_mandates SET status='active'`.
- **`ux_sub_mandates_company_active` (unique on `company_id WHERE status='active'`) stays the arbiter, and 23505 must never escape.** A company can reach a second completed authorisation (an abandoned checkout's Paystack access code stays payable), and in the webhook a throw rolls the whole event back, leaves `processed = FALSE`, answers 500 and makes every redelivery repeat forever with the card already charged. The activation is a conditional UPDATE in its own migration_admin transaction (S-07e), so a 23505 aborts only that transaction; the outcomes are `activated | already_active | already_active_other_code | not_pending | blocked`, and every outcome but the first two is a settled state that gets a `log.error` plus a `failure_reason` on the payment request — never a throw. Only `ux_sub_mandates_company_active` is absorbed: the 23505 handler matches the constraint NAME, so any other duplicate reaches the caller.
- A `revoked` / `expired` / `failed` mandate is never resurrected by a payment event (`not_pending`).
- **S-07e (migration 945): the billing tables are read-only to the app roles.** `flow_wallet`, `flow_ledger`, `flow_purchases`, `flow_bundles`, `plans`, `plan_features`, `feature_flags`, `company_feature_overrides`, `subscriptions`, `subscription_charges`, `subscription_mandates`: every write, row lock (`FOR UPDATE` needs UPDATE) and every read of `payment_method_token` or a mandate's/charge's `paystack_*` codes runs on `migrationAdminSqlTx` (`@/lib/auth/migrationAdminPool`), from a fixed statement keyed on a verified company or row id (that role bypasses RLS, so each names its `company_id`). Admin routes (`withAdmin`) keep their writes on platform_admin. A migration_admin write COMMITs before the request or webhook event does, so it is issued after the payment request's status change and is idempotent; a flow that must undo one calls the inverse (`withFlowMeter`/`mcp/flowMetering` refund on every failure exit, and register `runAfterRollback` so a request that rolls back after a 2xx is refunded; `mandate/create` marks an abandoned pending mandate `failed`). In the Paystack webhook those writes instead join a migration_admin transaction opened beside the event's (`publicRouteTx.ts`, `migrationAdmin: true`), committed just before it.
- **S-07e: `paystack_payment_requests` is app-written, so its link is a claim.** App roles may INSERT it and UPDATE only its status/checkout columns (945); no DELETE, no reading or writing the card codes. Before the webhook or mandate verify credits, settles, fails or activates anything, and before the webhook or the portal verify route books an invoice receipt, `linkMismatch` (`paystackLinkBinding.ts`) checks the request's company and purchase/charge/mandate/invoice against the checkout's Paystack metadata; a request with no link (a pre-651 mandate checkout) binds to nothing, since anyone can start a checkout with any metadata. A mismatch is logged and noted as `failure_reason = 'review:…'`, never thrown (a throw loops redelivery). An already-`completed` request (an app role may set `status`) takes the same bound, idempotent path, so a pre-emptive status write cannot cost a payment its credit. The charge cron logs when its reference already holds another request (`subscriptionChargeRequest.ts`). A credit needs at least the price (`requested_amount ?? amount`) in ZAR; a settle at least the charge's amount in ZAR.
- **The pre-651 fallback prefers the company's ALREADY-ACTIVE mandate** so a webhook redelivery resolves idempotently. That is only safe while the code matches: an active row carrying a DIFFERENT `paystack_authorization_code` means a SECOND checkout was paid, and it is reported `already_active_other_code`, never success.
- **`blocked` is never concluded from a stale read.** `verify` and the webhook are two observers of one transition, and the window between them is the outbound `verifyTransaction` call. The conditional UPDATE writing zero rows (or raising the 23505) does NOT identify which row holds the active slot: `reclassifyAfterNoUpdate` re-reads the row and reports `already_active` when the other observer activated it, `blocked` only when it is still pending.
- **`paystack_payment_requests.failure_reason` is read back, so a wrong one is durable and payer-visible.** `POST /api/billing/paystack/mandate/verify` answers `status: 'failed'` + `failureReason` when it is set, so a completed-but-unattached authorisation tells the payer to contact support instead of showing 'pending' forever — but a reason NEVER outranks this reference's own mandate being `active`, and a reason attached to a fallback resolution suppresses the whole mandate view (id, bank, card, ceiling), not just the id: the row it landed on belongs to another checkout.
- `POST /api/billing/flows/purchase` answers **503** when `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY` is absent: a missing gateway secret is an outage, not a free top-up. `ALLOW_UNPAID_FLOW_PURCHASE=true` opts a local/dev process into the admin-recorded fallback and is ignored when `NODE_ENV=production` (so every deployed environment ignores it).
- Mandate must be `active` AND have `stitch_bank_account_id` set; otherwise the charge is marked `failed` with `failure_reason='mandate_not_active'` (NB: the file-header comment says `'no_mandate'` — the runtime string is `'mandate_not_active'`, see `subscriptionBillingService.ts:181`).
- Subscription charge state: `queued → submitted | settled | failed | cancelled`. `failed` rows are retried up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS=3` with `RETRY_BACKOFF_HOURS=24` backoff; `runQueuedCharges` claims each attempt with a status- and attempt_count-predicated UPDATE, so two overlapping cron runs cannot both spend the same attempt.
- Mandate must be `active` AND have `paystack_authorization_code` set; otherwise the charge is marked `failed` with `failure_reason='mandate_not_active_or_missing_authorization'`.
- **The subscription period moves only on settlement**, never when a charge is queued. Every period/status write is keyed on `subscription_charges.subscription_id` (migration 624) — a company may hold several subscription rows, and keying on `company_id` alone made one charge move all of them. Charges predating 624 have a NULL `subscription_id` and move nothing.
- After `MAX_ATTEMPTS` failures the subscription is set `past_due` and no further charge is raised for that period. `past_due` currently gates no feature — dunning (suspend / notify) is not implemented.
- **A deleted company is not billed** (`companies.status = 'deleted'`, 2026-10-15): `generateDueCharges` skips its subscriptions and `runQueuedCharges` skips its charges. Delete/restore and the billing they do live in `admin/services/companyLifecycleService.ts` ("fresh start"): delete voids queued/failed charges for periods not yet granted (`failure_reason='company_deleted'`, same rule as `voidChargesForCancellingSubscriptions`) and keeps a granted-period debt, undebited while deleted; restore sets a lapsed active/past_due subscription's `current_period_end = now()`, so the next run raises one charge from today, not one per missed cycle (not restarted while a charge is `submitted` at Paystack; a restarted `cancel_at_period_end` subscription is closed out by the next run).
- **A payment request's invoice is its own company's.** `paystack_payment_requests` and `stitch_payment_requests` carry a composite FK `(customer_invoice_id, company_id)` -> `customer_invoices(id, company_id)` (migration 854, R-195), `ON DELETE SET NULL (customer_invoice_id)`. Write `company_id` from the invoice row (as `resolveLinkCharge` does), never from the session, or the insert fails 23503.

## Gotchas
- **A customer-invoice `charge.success` settles on what Paystack reports (R-181), not the request's
  `amount_cents`.** The handler passes `amount`, `currency`, `requested_amount` (the charge
  before a customer-paid fee) and `fees` to `recordGatewayInvoiceReceipt`; `verifyTransaction`
  maps the last two to `requestedAmountCents` and `feesCents`, and verify passes the same four. What is banked, flagged and fee-posted is decided in
  `accounting/services/ar` — see its `.claude.md`.
- **Recurring debits run through Paystack, not Stitch.** `runQueuedCharges` calls
  `paystackClient.chargeAuthorization` against the mandate's `paystack_authorization_code`; that
  path is live in production. The Stitch `debitFromMandate` stub in `stitchClient.ts` is a
  dependency-boundary guard for the ungranted `client_recurringpaymentconsentrequest` scope and is
  no longer on the subscription path — do not delete it or replace it with a fake success.
- **A charge stuck in `submitted` needs `resolveStaleSubmittedCharges`.** Only a webhook moves a
  charge out of `submitted`; the cron calls the resolver first each run so a charge whose webhook
  never arrived is verified against Paystack after `STALE_SUBMITTED_HOURS` and settled or failed.
- Stitch token cache is process-local; in serverless contexts each cold start re-auths. Acceptable today (low call volume).
- `flowOperationCatalog` is `as const satisfies Record<...>` — adding a new op code MUST update the type-narrowed map; do not push to it dynamically.
- The subscription lifecycle is covered by `tests/integration/k-033-*.int.test.ts` and `k-034-*.int.test.ts` (28 cases against the production schema, Paystack mocked) plus `tests/unit/services/billing/` and `tests/unit/api/admin-subscription-cancel-at-period-end.test.ts`. The Flow wallet and Stitch paths are still uncovered — do not read the subscription coverage as module-wide.
